narrative:
The model determined that you have a 35% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, your credit history, and the loan amount you requested. Your checking account status was the single biggest reason for the denial. Having between 0 and 200 DM in your account is relatively uncommon among approved applicants and pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. Your credit history rating of "critical or other credits" worked in the opposite direction. This is actually a fairly common profile among people who are approved, so it helped pull the prediction back toward approval. Finally, the amount you asked to borrow also increased the risk score. At 3617 DM, your request sits above the average amount granted to approved applicants, which added further weight toward denial.

Taken together, these factors led the model to conclude that the overall risk was too high. 

To improve your chances next time, focus on building a stronger checking account balance and reducing the size of any future loan requests. You may also want to review your full credit report to see if any past issues can be addressed. Once these areas look healthier, reapplying could produce a different result.
